 Wolves hold off Blazers late, take first of two-game set
 Nov 16, 2026 | 8:08 PM 
 Terrence Shannon Jr. scored 34 points on 8-for-11 shooting from the field and 15-for-16 shooting from the free-throw line, and the Minnesota Timberwolves held on for a 106-98 win over the Portland Trail Blazers on Monday night in Minneapolis.
 Rudy Gobert finished with 18 points and 15 rebounds for Minnesota, which picked up its sixth win in the past seven games. Jaden McDaniels and Jonathan Kuminga registered 13 points apiece.
 Deni Avdija scored 27 points on 11-for-19 shooting to lead Portland. Donovan Clingan recorded a double-double with 10 points and 10 rebounds, and Scoot Henderson and Jrue Holiday each chipped in 10 points off the bench.
 The teams will meet again Tuesday night in Minneapolis to complete a back-to-back set.
 The Timberwolves led by eight points at halftime and increased their advantage to 14 by the start of the fourth quarter. Shannon Jr. made a 3-pointer and two free throws to put Minnesota on top 87-70 late in the third quarter, and Jayson Kent knocked down a 3-pointer to bring Portland within 87-73 with 1.8 seconds remaining.
 The Trail Blazers closed the game on an 11-1 run but ran out of time to complete a comeback.
 Portland led by as many as 10 points in the first quarter.
 Clingan made an alley-oop dunk with 8:48 left in the opening session, and he followed with a tip-in layup about one minute later to put Portland on top 12-2.
 The Timberwolves responded with a 12-2 run to even the score at 24-all in the final minutes of the first quarter. Gobert made a pair of free throws and a reverse layup to start the run, which included two 3-pointers by Trey Lyles and one 3-pointer apiece by Ayo Dosunmu and Shannon Jr.
 Minnesota scored the final six points of the first half to grab an eight-point advantage at the break.
 McDaniels made a layup to put the Timberwolves on top 55-51 with 1:35 remaining in the half. Kuminga added a reverse dunk to make it 57-51 with 1:11 to go, and Shannon Jr. capped the first-half scoring when he drove for a layup with 53.7 seconds remaining.
